title: Penalty for intentionally deflecting a moving ball
question: What is the general penalty if a player deliberately stops or deflects a ball in motion?
explanation: A player who deliberately stops or deflects their own ball in motion receives the general penalty of two strokes.

juniorVersion.title: What happens if you stop your ball on purpose?
juniorVersion.question: If you hit your ball and then you or someone else purposely stops it or hits it while it is rolling, what is the usual penalty?
juniorVersion.explanation: If you or your caddie stop your ball on purpose after you hit it, you have to add 2 shots to your score. This is called the general penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This means you have to add 2 shots to your score for breaking a rule.
A person who helps you by carrying your clubs and giving advice.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Talk about why it is important to let the ball finish rolling without anyone trying to stop it on purpose.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think you only get 1 shot added, but it's 2 shots.
Some children might think it's okay for someone to stop the ball to help them, but it is not allowed.
